sections.heading: The idea
sections.body_md:
In equilibrium, carrier concentrations and electrostatic potential are locked together by the **Boltzmann relations**. Measure potential \(\varphi\) relative to intrinsic silicon: where \(\varphi\) is higher, electrons (attracted to high potential) are exponentially more plentiful and holes exponentially fewer.

This gives the handy **60 mV/decade rule**: every 60 mV of potential (more precisely \(\ln 10 \cdot kT/q \approx 60\ \mathrm{mV}\)) changes a carrier concentration by a factor of 10. An n-type region with \(n_0 = 10^{16}\) is 6 decades above \(n_i\), so it sits at about \(+360\ \mathrm{mV}\). A p-type region sits at a negative potential. The product \(np = n_i^2\) still holds everywhere in equilibrium.

sections.heading: Key equations
sections.body_md:
\[ n_0 = n_i\,e^{\varphi/V_{th}}, \qquad p_0 = n_i\,e^{-\varphi/V_{th}}, \qquad V_{th} = \frac{kT}{q} \approx 26\ \mathrm{mV} \]
\[ \varphi_n = V_{th}\ln\frac{N_D}{n_i}, \qquad \varphi_p = -V_{th}\ln\frac{N_A}{n_i} \]
Rule of thumb: \(\varphi \approx 60\ \mathrm{mV}\times\log_{10}(n_0/n_i)\).

sections.heading: Worked example
sections.body_md:
For p-type silicon with \(N_A = 10^{14}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}\):
\[ \varphi_p = -0.026\ln\frac{10^{14}}{10^{10}} = -0.026\cdot 9.21 \approx -0.24\ \mathrm{V} \]
The rule of thumb gives \(-60\ \mathrm{mV}\times4 = -240\ \mathrm{mV}\). ✓ Note the units: in this skill \(V_{th}\) is the thermal voltage, not a threshold voltage.

sections.heading: Common pitfalls
sections.body_md:
- Getting the sign wrong for p-type: holes are plentiful where \(\varphi\) is **negative**.
- Using \(\log_{10}\) with 26 mV; that pairing needs \(\ln\). Use 60 mV with \(\log_{10}\).
- Applying Boltzmann relations with bias applied, outside equilibrium.
- Confusing \(V_{th}\) (thermal voltage) with the MOS threshold voltage \(V_T\).

sections.heading: Where this leads
sections.body_md: These relations give the potential of each side of a PN junction, and therefore the built-in potential. They also set \(\varphi_p\) for a MOS body, which appears in the flat-band and threshold voltages.
